job: Document an API endpoint: parameters on the left, request and response on the right.
purpose: The reference page layout. The endpoint bar leads with the method and path; click the path to copy the URL. Prose and parameters sit on the left, and a sticky request and response panel on the right with a language picker and example picker. Try it opens a sheet built from the parameters, validates and shows a scripted response. Under 1100px the panels flow under the bar.
useWhen: An API reference needs the endpoint, its parameters and examples side by side.
Readers should try a call in a sandbox before writing code.

avoidWhen.when: A method and path shown inline in an app.
A form that runs one endpoint in the product.
A single code sample in prose.

states.name: error status
states.how: tone dot on 4xx and 5xx status tabs

parts.role: The full URL; click copies it.
A {param} in the path, emphasised in ink.
A list of parameter rows built on fd-schema.
One parameter: name, type, where, required, default, description.
The top of the page: article head and the endpoint bar.
The path button that copies the URL.

keyboard.does: Copies the endpoint path or opens a picker item.
Moves through pickers, parameters and the Try it fields.
